articleTitle: LCIs and synchronous motors applied to roller mills [load commutated invertors]
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: A cement company concerned about high power-factor penalty costs requested an evaluation of the feasibility of using synchronous motors starting through LCIs to drive three new roller mills at a cement plant. The prior experience with roller mills centered about the application of wound rotor induction motors with either cascaded secondary resistance or liquid rheostat. By utilizing synchronous motors, there was the possibility of providing leading power factor to reduce the reactive power demands seen by the utility feeding the cement plant. It was theorized that, if sufficient power factor correction could be obtained, the payback period of the incremental additional cost of the synchronous motor drive system would be very short. After payback of the initial investment, all future energy savings gravitate directly to the bottom line as additional revenue. Several key concerns had to be addressed in evaluating the use of synchronous motors for these relatively high starting torque requirement applications. This paper discusses the electrical and mechanical evaluation leading up to the decision to proceed with this new application of synchronous motors started through an LCI.

articleTitle: Ball mill drive motor choices
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The time has come to re-think the approach to mill drive motors because of the growth in size of newer ball mills, the starting torque restrictions of some of the newer mill drive configurations, and the softness of some utility services. This paper looks at the serviceability and economics of five different mill motor options to meet these restraints. Some approaches are new, some are old standards, and some, like the Phoenix, have risen from the ashes to return again.

articleTitle: Development status of a 1000 HP superconducting motor
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Following a successful demonstration of a 200 hp synchronous motor with a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) field winding, the effort continues on the development of a 1000 hp HTS motor. Under a contract with the Department of Energy, a vertically integrated team was formed for the development of large-stale industrial motors. The 1000 hp HTS motor has been strategically designed for operation from an adjustable-speed drive (ASD) using the same topology as the previously demonstrated 200 hp HTS motor (air-core AC synchronous motor with HTS field winding). It possesses all the essential features that can be scaled up to a pre-commercial prototype rated at 5000 hp. Successful demonstration of this motor will bring the HTS motor technology to a critical point where HTS motors will be comparable in size and efficiency to conventional high efficiency motors. Completion of the 1000 hp HTS motor will be followed by the development of a precommercial unit (5000 hp) to demonstrate the full benefits of HTS motors by saving half the losses of conventional motors in a package with half the volume. This paper reviews the overall design characteristics of a 1000 hp HTS motor and summarizes the development status of the motor system including its cryogenic refrigeration system.

articleTitle: The installation of an advanced power management system for reduced operating and maintenance expense in a cement mill
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: PC based power management systems implemented in conjunction with the latest microprocessor based protective relays have enabled power distribution system operators and owners to view and understand the operating dynamics of their systems in new and unique ways. The multifunctional relays and meters have enabled a reduction in the number of components and increased the reliability of the power distribution systems. The PC based software allows for setpoint adjustments, parameter trending, waveform analysis, and event recording with time-date stamping. This paper reviews the design and installation, field experience, derived benefits of, and plans for expansion of a system installed at a cement plant. The system includes features such as an interactive one-line diagram that can show system parameters at a glance, monitoring of the 69 kV, 13.2 kV, and 4.16 kV distribution systems, as well as the large synchronous ball mill and other medium voltage motors utilized in the cement manufacture process.

articleTitle: Kiln alignment analysis-an overview of the direct method
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Hot kiln alignment has been with us more than a decade now. The innovation for aligning kilns while in operation brings with it the promise of analyzing its mechanics in a dynamic setting. In doing so, the procedure does not conflict with production or shut down periods. Hot alignment analysis then truly becomes the preventive maintenance tool it was always meant to be. The ability to measure kiln alignment "hot" resulted from new measurement technology and of course the introduction of portable computing power into the industrial environment about two decades ago. The method described in this paper is based on a fundamentally new approach, alignment by centers of rotation. This is an innovation not in measurement hardware but in the basic approach to the task. Alignment by centers of rotation was accepted in patents in the USA, the European Community Countries (EC) and several other countries. The method derives the state of alignment by direct and continuous noncontact measurement to the rotating kiln shell, rather than the usual measurement of diameters and other parameters of the kiln rollers and tires.

articleTitle: The cross-bar cooler: innovative and proven
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The cross-bar cooler was first introduced to the cement industry in 1997. After nearly 3 1/2 years of operating experience and 17 new coolers sold to date, this technology is both revolutionary and proven. This paper highlights four innovative design features of the cross-bar cooler and presents the physical size, process efficiency, philosophy of operation, energy consumption and fan requirements for cooling 5000 MTPD of clinker from 1400/spl deg/C to 100/spl deg/C. In this regard, the cooler is the supplier's normal design. In fact, coolers of the same size, as chosen for this application and as presented herein, have already been delivered.

articleTitle: Separate slag grinding in different milling systems
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The variation in power required to grind slag is about the same as that required for ordinary portland cement. It is although, generally at a higher power level than that required for cement for the same Blaine values. In addition, to produce products having similar strengths, slag must be ground to a higher Blaine than that for normal portland cement. When the effects of inter-grinding of the two materials is taken into account, there is definitely a case made for the separate grinding of the two materials simultaneously, while grinding and blending the two different materials. Excess energy may be expended on one, and insufficient energy on the other in this type of process. When they are ground separately it is easier to control the beneficial qualities of the two different materials. This allows also utilization of the least expensive production process for each material.

articleTitle: Thermal imaging and predictive maintenance: what the future has in store
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Advancement in infrared detector technology has made significant progress. Whilst there is still good reason to use single element detectors to achieve the high spatial resolution required for remote kiln shell line scanning, infrared focal plane array based thermal imaging systems bring new benefits to thermal imaging used within the cement plant. Lower costs and easier to use equipment with simple to use software open up many opportunities for plants to perform their own predictive and preventive maintenance. This provides more flexibility and faster return on capital as they can conveniently utilise the equipment for preventive and diagnostic use instead of being wholly dependent on third parties or consultants. Focal plane array based infrared cameras are now being brought into new roles within the entire plant including inside the kiln itself, where they can bring both imaging and measurement benefits that improve process control, operational efficiency and energy costs.

articleTitle: No bearing problems [cement industry MV motors]
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Bearing heavy loads is difficult for bearings as well as for people. To minimise the load bearings are exposed to, the authors describe how it is important to be familiar with the characteristics of the two used bearing types, the operation mode planned and also the maintenance requirements of the bearing itself.

articleTitle: Modern clinker cooler technology
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Today, the importance of the clinker cooler for the efficiency of the kiln process is generally known. The special challenge in cooler design is to combine aspects like plating, aeration, grate line design, grate support and other mechanical aspects into a complete technical solution, offering maximum mechanical and thermal performance. The specific challenges of the cooling process are described and technical solutions to meet these with modern cooler design are illustrated. On the example of a fictitious 5000 mt/d clinker cooler, its design features, operating parameters as well as electrical and mechanical equipment is presented. Furthermore, the influence of clinker size distribution on the cooling process is presented in form of results of a computer simulation program.

articleTitle: Technical advancements in automation of cement dispatch terminals
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Cost-effective conveyance, bagging, palletizing, packaging and loading in the cement industry requires plants, which are developed within a consistent overall plan. Preferably, a complete system with all components being acquired from a single supplier and has to guarantee: (1) a high level of availability; (2) increase of dispatch capacity; (3) reduction of operating costs; (4) acceleration of cash flow; (5) quality control and assurance; and (6) functionality of a turn-key project. This paper shows an example of automating dispatch procedures. The individual components as well as the functions of the dispatch automation are specified and described in detail.

articleTitle: Intelligent motor control centers (IMCCs)-the present and future
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Device-level integration through digital communication is the key to unlocking the full potential in the electronic controls being installed in industrial plants today. Users in all industries are seeking solutions that integrate software, hardware and communication technologies to deliver plant-floor benefits such as improved process control and diagnostics and increased reliability. The development and packaging of new technologies in device-level communication and sensing capabilities, along with dedicated software, enable intelligent control architectures to provide both abundant real-time process information, as well as predictive maintenance information to further improve productivity.

articleTitle: Opportunities for cement plants in the changing electricity industry
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Electricity has had and will continue to have an important impact on our society. The availability of reliable supplies at affordable prices has made possible the high standard of living and level of industrial development we enjoy today. The electricity industry in the United States is going through the process of deregulation. This paper discusses the regulation history of the electricity industry, the concepts of deregulation, an understanding of the benefits therein and how those changes will apply to the cement industry. It will definitely not be business as usual-the cement industry is an energy intensive industry and electricity pricing contributes heavily to its costs. The "New World" will be very complex, but will yield opportunities for cost savings for the cement industry.

articleTitle: Design features of the BMH Claudius Peters cooler the new swing support grate cooler
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: During the last 20 years, clinker cooler techniques have changed tremendously regarding process requirements as well as mechanical design and control aspects. The main objectives are the optimal integration of the cooler into the pyro-process of the cement production line and the reduction of the overall production costs. The paper provides a detailed introduction of the new, unique features of the BMH Claudius Peters Grate Cooler, which have been newly developed, installed and are in operation.

articleTitle: Alternative project execution approaches
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Depending on the specific conditions of a given project, there are a number of alternatives available to the project owner for the execution approach. On the basis of the allocation of risks to the project participants, these options range from one extreme in which one contractor takes full responsibility for the project execution (full turnkey) to the other extreme in which the owner takes full control of the project for its implementation (full multiple contracting). Between these two extremes there are a number of other execution approaches that have been used in which the total project risk is shared between the owner and the contractors in varying proportions. Some specific project factors may influence the decision on the approach to be used, in particular the experience and resources of the project owner, the project time table, the scope of the project, the local conditions and other factors. This paper presents a review of these alternative approaches, along with a discussion of the influence of the above factors on the decision of the approach to be used. A brief outline of some important trends in the construction industry in North America is also presented, along with a discussion on their potential impact on the project performance.

articleTitle: Cement kiln baghouse 20 year life cycle comparison jet pulse vs. reverse air
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to provide a systematic way of evaluating both jet pulse and reverse air cement kiln baghouse technologies for the volume ranges where the decision making process is difficult because some of the data that should influence this process are not readily available. The authors also provide a way to measure the operational cost impact over a 20 year life cycle. The tables and graphs provided should be interpreted not so much in absolute dollar value as in relative numbers. Since all the units have been sized with the same basic criteria, any cost differential due to particular site conditions are assumed to have the same financial impact in both cases.

articleTitle: Replacement kit for cement mill gearboxes
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Improvements to cement mill operation via installation of planetary gearboxes as "replacement kits", have recently proven to be very successful, due to quick return on investments thanks to the immediate achievement of higher efficiency and improvement in mill operation. The installation of a "replacement kit" gearbox in most cases includes the utilization of the existing foundation by installation of "tailor made" intermediate frame or adaptation to the gearbox casing. With this concept of customized solutions, the cement plant saves time and money, as the erection time of the new "replacement kit" gearbox is limited to a time frame of maximum 2-3 weeks. Cost optimization is further achieved by possible utilization of the existing auxiliary drives as well as no running in time. Finally, no displacement of the main motor is required due to the compact design of the 2-stage planetary gearbox. The overall improvement in service life for cement mill "replacement kits" gearboxes along with optimization of maintenance cost, is shown based on actual recent installations.

articleTitle: Design features of the Polysius clinker cooler
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The most important aspect of clinker cooler operation, which directly affects the overall performance delivered, is that of clinker distribution over the width of the cooler. With an optimal distribution, red rivers and blow-throughs can be minimized; the result of which is maximum heat recovery and availability. Over the years, Polysius has provided 78 REPOL(R) clinker coolers, and modified an additional 29 units. With regard to the example cooler presented, Polysius has supplied 18 such coolers for capacities of at least 5,000 mtpd clinker.

articleTitle: Modernization of the Richmond cement plant
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Lafarge Canada's Richmond cement plant modernisation is discussed. The construction site is described as are the technical features of the plant. The power and control modernisation was a retrofit project and is discussed. A new kiln line was installed and its startup is briefly described. The initial performance of the modernised plant is outlined.

articleTitle: "On line particle size analyzer" at Ash Grove's Leamington Utah Plant
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Cement plants are looking at automating the myriad of things to cut production costs and improve quality. In the QC department at the Leamington Plant a decision was made to use the newly developed online light scattering technology to control cement fineness. The online analyzer installation contributed to a record cement production year in 1999 by tightening control of the cement fineness. In November of 1998 a real time particle size analyzer was purchased from Malvern/Insitec and installed on the finish milling system. This paper describes the online analyzer and its implementation at the plant. The operating experience with the analyzer is discussed.

articleTitle: Fall of ground and haul truck fatalities in the limestone industry
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: This paper examines fatalities related to the haulage and fall-of-ground incidents in the limestone industry over the past three years. A high incident rate has caused the US Mines Safety and Health Administration to focus heavily on enforcement procedures. A close look at each fatality and an examination of the federal mine safety standards relating to each incident is discussed. Policy and procedure recommendations that can be implemented by management to prevent future occurrence are included.

articleTitle: Environmental issues associated with the permitting process for TXI's modernization of their Midlothian, Texas cement plant
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: An important step in any expansion project is obtaining an air permit. Obviously, it is quicker to obtain an air permit via the replacement of existing equipment with new modern equipment versus the building of a green-field plant. The shorter permit attainment time is generally linked to the ability to "net out" in emissions. With respect to cement plants, the term "netting out" refers to no increases in emissions of particulate, nitrogen oxides (NO/sub x/), sulfur oxides (SO/sub x/), and carbon monoxide (CO). TXI chose to evaluate the feasibility of expanding their Midlothian Cement Plant. The purpose of this paper is to discuss the permitting strategy associated with the expansion of TXI Midlothian Cement from 1.2 million stons (1.09 million mtons) of clinker to 2.8 million stons (2.5 million mtons). This permitting strategy led to the replacement of two, 900 sTPD (816 mTPD) long wet kilns with a 6,000 sTPD (5,443 mTPD) modern 4-stage preheater/precalciner kiln without an increase in emissions. In order to "net out" in particulate emissions, state of the art dust collector technology had to be used. Dust collectors for the new plant and part of the existing facility had to incorporate membrane bags in their design. In order to "net out" in sulfur emissions, a wet sulfur scrubber was considered in the design of the new kiln line. In order to "net out" in NO/sub x/ emissions, the new kiln line was installed with low NO/sub x/ calciner technology. In order to "net out" in CO emissions, a regenerative thermal oxidizer (RTO) with 95% thermal energy recovery was incorporated into the design. It is important to note that this is the first application of RTO technology in a cement plant. The general arrangement of the sulfur scrubber and the RTO is shown.

articleTitle: Ball mill driven with gearless mill drive
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: This paper introduces how PT Semen Bosowa/Indonesia considered the installation of a cement plant gearless mill drive, the criteria for the selection of the gearless mill drive versus traditional solutions, the technology developed for this particular application and the conclusion drawn from this experience.

articleTitle: The IKN pendulum cooler
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The pendulum cooler is designed in close accordance with the cross flow principle. The clinker bed in a pendulum cooler is characterized by a temperature profile and vertical segregation of particles. In a profiled clinker bed, the difference in temperature between gas and solid is maximized. Horizontal air jets simulate an infinite number of openings in the grate surface. By pressurizing the voids or interstices in the clinker bed the cooling air sweeps the fluidizable fines to the bed surface. Only when the voids are completely purged, the pressure drop of the bed is at a minimum. In a pendulum cooler, the movable portion of the grate is suspended on long and inclined strands of metal sheets. The fixed and movable frames are designed to limit deflection to one millimeter variation of gaps under full load. The grate surface consists of Coanda nozzles with replaceable blades, which generate horizontal air jets. This paper describes the design of the pendulum cooler and its main components.

articleTitle: Modular lining for clinker coolers
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: The exponential increase in kiln capacity, coupled with a corresponding increase in cooler heat recovery efficiency poses a new challenge to refractory linings around the kiln hood and cooler. With it came a sharp increase in secondary air temperature, an increase in alkali and sulphur concentration and an increase in buildup formation. These new conditions are responsible for frequent refractory failures. Pre-cast, fired shapes, the main subject of this paper, are not new to the cement industry. The technical literature refers to preheaters lined with precast moduli as far back as 1983. In the United States, the author's experience with this concept started in 1989, with two cooler linings in New York State. What makes this old concept so attractive today are the increased thermal and chemical stresses posed by high-efficiency clinker coolers and high capacity kilns. This paper compares several cooler lining alternatives to pre-cast, pre-fired shapes.

articleTitle: Bulk cement ship and barge unloading systems, which system is best?
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: During the 1990s, economic circumstances have encouraged the development of new water based bulk material terminals in many parts of the world. This has become increasingly the case in the USA during the latter part of the 1990s, when cement shortages have caused bulk cement to become one of the major import commodities for many bulk terminals. Because of the physical nature of cement, the process of unloading it from ships or barges can present a major hurdle in the path of the implementation of a cement unloading terminal. The purpose of this paper is to analyze the advantages and disadvantages of the four unloading systems that are available (mechanical screw unloader, pneumatic unloader, self discharging ships, and grab bucket and hopper unloaders), and to help the reader to better understand which system may work best for their specific application.

articleTitle: A comparison of liquid-filled and dry-type transformer technologies
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: This paper assembles data from various sources in order to provide information to evaluate liquid-filled and dry-type transformers. The first basis of comparison is a general product description of product development and design. The second comparison is a specific comparison of electrical characteristics based on standard and optional ratings. A general description of industry standards with their prevailing focus as well specific references to the applicable industry standards for the products being compared in this review is also provided. The comparison of kilovolt-ampere (kVA) sizes and voltages is based on distribution ratings most commonly used in the United States. Only ANSI and NEMA standards are used as references for the electrical characteristic comparison.

articleTitle: Next generation controllers for kiln/cooler and mill applications based on model predictive control and neural networks
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has become the standard supervisory control tool in some process industries, including oil refining and petrochemicals. It has been introduced into the cement industry, in a kiln/cooler application at Pretoria Portland Cement's (PPC) Dwaalboom plant in South Africa. This application differs from the well-established expert system approach in that it incorporates a model of the process rather than a model of the operator. The continuous regulation and disturbance rejection of MPC is well suited to kiln/cooler control, and for example the application recovers from major upsets such as coating drop three times faster than typical operator intervention. Mills have been known to demonstrate severe nonlinear behavior, and linear controllers in mill applications have yielded only varying degrees of success. Most applications are eventually turned off due to poor performance caused by this nonlinear behaviour. Nonlinear MPC has been applied to the cement mill at Dwaalboom-a closed circuit ball mill. Gains are calculated at each control execution using a neural network model built from three months of log sheet data. Gains in the controller change by as much as a factor of fifteen. This controller has demonstrated significantly improved setpoint tracking and disturbance rejection over all three-product grades.

articleTitle: Series connected circuit breakers, test and know
publicationTitle: 2000 IEEE-IAS/PCA Cement Industry Technical Conference. Conference Record (Cat. No.00CH37047)
abstract: Series rated circuit breakers are commonplace, but not always well understood. This paper provides basic information on how a series rating is tested and relates that information to the action of the overcurrent protective devices involved. The paper also explores the question of whether calculations can be used to determine the series rating of an untested combination.
